root_cause.text: In the cpcap-battery driver, `devm_` IRQ registration was done before `devm_` power-supply registration, so reverse-order managed cleanup and probe-time interrupt delivery allowed the IRQ handler to call `power_supply_changed()` on an uninitialized or already freed `power_supply` handle.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(pdev, ddata)` from before the power-supply setup to after it, and the CVE/commit text explicitly states that requesting the IRQ first causes the `power_supply` handle to be freed before the IRQ handler is unregistered during removal, and can also let an interrupt fire before the handle is registered during probe.

intent_record.intent_summary: Remove interrupt initialization from cpcap_battery_probe() so probe no longer performs or fails on that setup step.
intent_record.what: The probe function cpcap_battery_probe() was modified to remove the call to cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(pdev, ddata) and the subsequent error check and early return based on its result, leaving the following initialization step cpcap_battery_init_iio(ddata) unchanged.
intent_record.how: At runtime, the battery driver probe no longer initializes interrupts at this point and will not fail probe due to an error returned from cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(). This changes initialization flow by skipping that interrupt setup step entirely in this function.

intent_record.intent_summary: Initialize battery interrupts during probe and fail early if setup does not succeed.
intent_record.what: A call to cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(pdev, ddata) was added in cpcap_battery_probe(), along with storing its return value in error and immediately returning if the call fails, before atomic_set(&ddata->active, 1) and battery calibration.
intent_record.how: At probe time, the driver now initializes battery-related interrupts earlier and aborts device setup if that initialization fails. This ensures interrupt handling is set up before the device is marked active and before calibration proceeds, preventing the driver from continuing with incomplete interrupt configuration.

relevance_review.reason: Removing IRQ initialization from probe directly affects the vulnerable ordering/cleanup path: it prevents probe-time IRQ registration and delivery from occurring before power-supply registration, which is the root cause of the unsafe power_supply_changed() access.

The change directly affects probe-time IRQ setup ordering/behavior by initializing battery interrupts during probe and failing early on setup errors, which is tied to the root cause of interrupts being registered and potentially delivered before the power-supply object was safely available.

candidates.rationale: This probe-time call performs the IRQ registration too early. Because devm cleanup unwinds in reverse registration order, registering IRQs before the power_supply object allows the IRQ handler to run before power_supply registration completes or after the power_supply has already been freed during teardown.

vuln_statements.explanation: This statement performs interrupt initialization during probe before the managed power_supply registration is established. Because devm resources are released in reverse order, this ordering lets the IRQ handler outlive or race ahead of the power_supply object, enabling power_supply_changed() to act on an uninitialized or freed handle.

bic_trace_step.reason: The vulnerable ordering is clearly present in `cpcap_battery_probe()`. The probe calls `cpcap_battery_init_interrupts(pdev, ddata);` before registering the power supply with `ddata->psy = devm_power_supply_register(ddata->dev, psy_desc, &psy_cfg);`. Inside `cpcap_battery_init_irq()`, IRQs are registered with `devm_request_threaded_irq(ddata->dev, irq, NULL, cpcap_battery_irq_thread, IRQF_SHARED, name, ddata);`, meaning managed IRQ cleanup will run after later-managed resources are freed, and the IRQ can also fire during probe before `ddata->psy` is initialized. The IRQ handler `cpcap_battery_irq_thread()` unconditionally executes `power_supply_changed(ddata->psy);` after checking only `atomic_read(&ddata->active)`. Since `atomic_set(&ddata->active, 1);` is done only after `devm_power_supply_register()`, probe-time delivery is somewhat gated until the end, but the root-cause cleanup ordering bug still exists: IRQs are devm-registered earlier than the devm power-supply object, so on teardown the power supply can be freed before IRQ release. There is no explicit fix here such as registering the power supply before IRQs, freeing IRQs before power-supply teardown, or guarding `power_supply_changed()` against an uninitialized/freed `psy`.
